summary: This note profiles José Rafael Abello Silva, known as "Mono Abello," a top-ranking member of Colombia's Medellín Cartel. He was reputed to run the cartel's Caribbean coast operations and was counted among major drug traffickers in the Santa Marta region. In January 1987 he was captured in Barranquilla after being named in a list of 128 narcotics figures ordered captured by President Virgilio Barco, but he was released soon after, apparently with help from senator Miguel Pinedo Barros.
one_line: Profile of José Rafael Abello Silva, a Medellín Cartel figure who ran Caribbean coast operations and was freed after a 1987 capture.
key_facts: José Rafael Abello Silva, alias "Mono Abello", was a top-ranking member of Colombia's Medellín Cartel.
Abello was considered among the major drug traffickers in the Santa Marta region.
He was the reputed chief of Caribbean coast operations on behalf of the Medellín Cartel.
During January 1987, José Rafael Abello Silva was included in a group of 128 major narcotics figures whose capture was ordered by President Virgilio Barco.
José Rafael Abello Silva was captured in Barranquilla in January 1987.
José Rafael Abello Silva was released shortly after his capture in Barranquilla.
His release was apparently achieved with the help of Miguel Pinedo Barros.
Miguel Pinedo Barros was a senator in La Guajira and was reputed to be a protector of cocaine traffickers.
Virgilio Barco was the President who ordered the capture of 128 major narcotics figures in January 1987.
The Medellín Cartel was a notorious Colombian drug trafficking organization.
